target: While proportional-only tuning a database autoscaler, the team increased gain until the closed loop showed sustained constant-amplitude oscillation. That boundary gain was 6 and the oscillation period was 8 minutes. They now need concrete classic PID gains (parallel form Kp, Ki, Kd) from this ultimate-cycle experiment, rather than continuing ad hoc gain changes.
surface: A previous autoscaler backed off to half the oscillation-boundary proportional gain, set Kp=3, and left integral and derivative gains at zero.
structural: A chemical process used the classic Ziegler-Nichols ultimate-gain PID rule. From ultimate gain Ku and period Pu it set Kp=0.6Ku, integral time Ti=Pu/2, derivative time Td=Pu/8; in parallel form Ki=Kp/Ti and Kd=Kp*Td.
rubric: Explicitly selects the classic Ziegler-Nichols ultimate-cycle PID tuning rule.
Uses Ku=6, Pu=8 to compute Kp=0.6*6=3.6, Ti=4, Td=1.
Converts to parallel gains Ki=3.6/4=0.9 and Kd=3.6*1=3.6.
Recommends (Kp,Ki,Kd)=(3.6,0.9,3.6) as the classic starting gains rather than proportional-only Kp=3.
Notes this aggressive heuristic assumes a suitable stable loop/consistent units and requires validation or detuning.
